messages:
matt (eng-platform): quick sync — running into inconsistent surface when runtime falls back to a cheaper model variant. some clients get 503, others get 200 with an "error" field. we need a consistent contract so SDKs and console can show an actionable hint.

matt (eng-platform): example of what i've seen from two internal services:
```
HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
{\n  "message": "capacity constrained, fallback failed"\n}
```
vs
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
{\n  "error": "fallback_used",\n  "note": "response generated by small-ffn-quant model",\n  "retry_after": 60\n}
```

matt (eng-platform): @jessica tagging you b/c SDK currently treats 200 as success and skips surfaced hints. we should standardize.

jessica (devex): agreed. right now SDK maps by HTTP code only. changing that is breaking but doable if we add a header or stable field. prefer machine-friendly header over parsing freeform "note".

offen (typo) owen (eng-runtime): fwiw runtime intentionally returns 200 for successful responses even if they came from fallback variants; we attach structured metadata in the body under `routing_meta`. example:
```
{\n  "output": "...",\n  "routing_meta": {\n    "variant": "small-ffn-quant",\n    "reason": "latency_target_violation",\n    "fallback": true\n  }\n}
```

ow: but i see the problem — SDKs and customers expect determinism.

sana (product): product concern: customers should get a concise, user-friendly hint when behavior changes, plus a telemetry-safe machine signal. proposal: keep 200 for responses, but add `X-Redwood-Routing-Info` header (json-encoded or compact) + `Retry-After` if retryable. the console can then surface a short message like: "We returned a lower-capacity variant to preserve latency".

jessica (devex): header sounds good. SDK changes: map header -> event; keep current success path but emit `warning` event if header indicates fallback or quota soft-limit. we can expose `response.warning` with a short string and `response.warning_code` for programmatic checks.

matt (eng-platform): also need to separate quota signals: soft quota (best-effort fallback) vs hard quota (reject). we shouldn't use the same status for both. suggest: hard quota -> 429; soft quota -> 200 + header `X-Redwood-Quota-State: soft` and `X-Redwood-Quota-Remaining` numeric.

owen (eng-runtime): agree. runtime will emit telemetry tags: `routed_variant`, `route.reason`, and `quota.state` so we can filter in Console. important: preserve `request_id` in headers for linking traces.

sana (product): Rollout UX: show a per-route timeline in Console that records when fallbacks started and the percentage of requests routed to fallback. also include a canned user-facing sentence we can show in apps: "Degraded response returned to meet latency targets; content may be lower-fidelity." optional link to docs.

jessica (devex): here's a tiny SDK pseudocode mapping proposal we can include in the changelog:
```
if (status == 429) throw QuotaExceededError;
else if (header['x-redwood-quota-state'] == 'soft') {
  emitWarning('quota_soft_limit', {remaining: header['x-redwood-quota-remaining']});
}
else if (header['x-redwood-routing-info']) {
  info = parse(header['x-redwood-routing-info']);
  emitWarning(info.code || 'fallback_used', {variant: info.variant});
}
```

jessica (devex): keep the public string short. SDK can expand into human-readable text based on locale.

errorbot: [deploy-bot] change applied to runtime canary: routing-meta -> header encoding enabled (canary: us-west-2, 5%). :white_check_mark:

matt (eng-platform): action items: 1) runtime: add `X-Redwood-Routing-Info` and `X-Redwood-Quota-State` headers + ensure `request_id` preserved (owen). 2) devex: add SDK mapping + warning API, changelog & migration guide (jessica). 3) product: console UX for fallback timeline + built-in canned sentence + docs (sana). 4) telemetry: expose routed_variant and route.reason tags (owen).

matt (eng-platform): can everyone ack (or flag blockers) by EOD? i'd like to roll to broader canary next week. :clock1:
